properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 10:00AM EDT until October 11 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...In Northeast Georgia, the following counties: Elbert,
Franklin, Habersham, Hart, Rabun and Stephens. In western North
Carolina, the following counties: Avery, Buncombe, Burke, Caldwell,
McDowell, Polk,  Rutherford, Haywood, Henderson, Macon, Mitchell,
Jackson, Transylvania and Yancey. In Upstate South Carolina, the
following counties: Abbeville, Anderson, Central Greenville,
Greater Oconee, Greater Pickens, Greenville, Greenwood, Laurens,
Spartanburg, and Oconee.

* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings
may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- As Isaias weakens and moves northward through the Mid-South this
morning, periods of rain will continue. Rainfall rates will
increase during the day, and heavy rain is most likely this
afternoon through early Sunday morning, particularly along the
south and east facing Blue Ridge Escarpment, that is, near the
southern border of North Carolina west of I-26, and in the sharp
terrain from near Saluda to Grandfather Mountain in North
Carolina. Also, a slow-moving band of heavy rain may move across
northeast Georgia and the Upstate of South Carolina late this
afternoon and evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Watch for flash flooding means there is a potential for rapid
onset flooding based on current forecasts. Flash flooding is a very
dangerous situation and may impact areas that do not typically flood.
Please monitor the latest forecasts and be prepared to take action
quickly should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Rainfall of more than five inches in similar storms has been
associated with an increased risk of landslides, especially
fast-moving debris flows and debris slides. If you live on a
mountainside or in a cove at the base of a mountain, especially near
a stream, be ready to leave in advance of the storm and follow
evacuation orders from local officials. Consider postponing travel
along mountain roads during the heavy rainfall event.

* WHAT...East winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph expected.

* WHERE...Portions of east Tennessee and southwest Virginia.

* WHEN...Until 8 AM EDT /7 AM CDT/ Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Localized gusts up to 50 mph possible.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

NWSheadline: WIND ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 AM EDT /7 AM CDT/ SUNDAY

properties.areaDesc: Taylor, FL
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 9:22AM EDT until October 10 at 11:15AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...North Central Taylor County in Big Bend Florida...

* WHEN...Until 1115 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 921 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Perry, Hampton Springs, Perry-Foley Airport, Bucell Junction,
Secotan and Boyd.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 1115 AM EDT THIS MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Northern Susitna Valley
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 10 at 5:13AM AKDT until October 11 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow. Total snow accumulations 4 to 12 inches.

* WHERE...Broad Pass.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An early season snowfall is expected for Broad
Pass through Sunday morning. Steady snow this morning may mix with
rain and taper off for a time this afternoon before changing back
to all snow Saturday evening through Sunday morning. Snow totals
will be highly dependent on temperatures with daytime highs in the
lower to mid 30s. 2 to 8 inches of snow is likely with the first
round of snow this morning and another 2 to 4 inches with the
second round later tonight into Sunday morning.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

NWSheadline: WINTER WEATHER ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 7 AM AKDT SUNDAY

properties.areaDesc: Cherokee; Clay; Sequatchie; Bledsoe; Rhea; Meigs; Marion; Hamilton; Bradley; West Polk; East Polk
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 9:10AM EDT until October 11 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Morristown TN
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest North Carolina, including the
following areas, Cherokee and Clay and east Tennessee, including
the following areas, Bledsoe, Bradley, East Polk, Hamilton, Marion,
Meigs, Rhea, Sequatchie and West Polk.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Remnants of Hurricane Isaias is expected to bring moderate to
heavy rainfall to the area this morning through early Sunday.
Rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches with locally heavier amounts
possible. The potential for repeated rounds of moderate to heavy
rain will support the potential of flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SUNDAY MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Coastal waters from Edisto Beach SC to Savannah GA out 20 NM; Coastal waters from Savannah GA to Altamaha Sound GA out 20 nm, including Grays Reef National Marine Sanctuary; Waters from Edisto Beach SC to Savannah GA extending from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from Savannah GA to Altamaha Sound GA extending from 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 10 at 9:09AM EDT until October 10 at 11:15AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
SMWCHS

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Edisto Beach SC to Savannah GA out 60 NM...
Waters from Savannah GA to Altamaha Sound GA out 60 NM...

* Until 1115 AM EDT.

* At 909 AM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 5 NM east of Buoy L, moving northeast at 15
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 34 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Hilton Head Reef, Betsy Ross Reef, Buoy L, Dredge Henry, Latex
Barge, Sayler Barge, Tug Delta Diamond, Tug Senasqua, Beaufort 45
Feet Reef, Tug Matt Turecamo, General Gordon, C C A Buoy, 110
Degree Olympic Buoy and Hunting Island Reef.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 10 at 9:09AM EDT until October 10 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 15 to 20 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and
seas 5 to 8 ft.

* WHERE...Offshore Gulf waters from the Walton-Okaloosa County
line to the Ochlockonee River from 20 to 60 nautical miles
out, Nearshore Gulf waters from the Ochlockonee River to the
Suwannee River out 20 nautical miles, St. Andrews Bay
Waterways, Coastal waters from Mexico Beach to Okaloosa Walton
County Line FL out 20 NM, Coastal waters from Mexico Beach to
Apalachicola FL out 20 NM, and Coastal Waters From Ochlockonee
River to Apalachicola Fl out to 20 Nm.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM EDT /4 PM CDT/ this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20
to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to
produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous
conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering
response, broaching, overturned dinghies and kayaks, slips and
falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,
and dragging anchors.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.

NWSheadline: SMALL CRAFT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 5 PM EDT /4 PM CDT/ THIS AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Conecuh, AL; Covington, AL; Crenshaw, AL; Escambia, AL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 10 at 7:55AM CDT until October 10 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall from Hurricane Isaias
continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Conecuh County in south central Alabama...
Covington County in south central Alabama...
Southern Crenshaw County in south central Alabama...
Eastern Escambia County in south central Alabama...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Expect many
areas of slow moving or standing water. It will take several hours
for all the water from these storms to work through local drainage
systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 754 AM CDT, Residual flooding continues from heavy rain that
fell from Hurricane Isaias. Between 6 and 12 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Andalusia, Opp, Brewton, Florala, East Brewton, Brantley, River
Falls, Red Level, Lockhart, Dozier, Heath, Gantt, Glenwood,
Riverview, Carolina, Beck, Stanley, Red Oak, Loango and Rhump.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM CDT THIS MORNING

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 10 at 7:53AM CDT until October 10 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall from Hurricane Isaias
continues.

* WHERE...Okaloosa County in northwestern Florida...
Santa Rosa County in northwestern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall. It
will take several hours for all the water from these storms to work
through local drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 753 AM CDT, broadcast media reported heavy rain in the warned
area from Hurricane Isaias. Flooding is already occurring.
Between 6 and 12 inches of rain have fallen.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wright, Fort Walton Beach, Crestview, Niceville, Destin, Eglin
AFB, Milton, Valparaiso, Mary Esther, Bagdad, Ocean City, Lake
Lorraine, Baker, Navarre, Shalimar, Laurel Hill, Cinco Bayou,
Roeville, Point Baker and Navarre Beach.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 10 at 4:51AM AKDT until October 11 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Snow begins Saturday morning then becomes
heavier Saturday night with total snow accumulations up to 8 inches
by Sunday evening. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph may result in
areas of blowing snow.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range South of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 4 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...An early season snowfall is expected late tonight through
Sunday. Roads and especially bridges are likely to become slick and
snow covered.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.
